fichas.title: Open-plan offices
fichas.summary: Open-plan offices are described as suitable for large groups doing shared work and routine activities requiring relatively little concentration. The text discusses their historical rationale and drawbacks, including long room depths, high building-services costs, limited conversion flexibility, social control, and optical and acoustic disturbance.
uses: Routine activities with a low concentration threshold

dimensions.label: Room depth
dimensions.context: Extensive room depths associated with open-plan offices

cross_refs: Mies van der Rohe: '... clearly laid-out, undivided, only structured ...' (→ refs)

fichas.title: Single-room offices
fichas.summary: Single-room offices suit independent or concentrated work, either by one person or by very small groups that need to exchange information constantly. The text notes their use in Germany since World War II and their continuing suitability where workplace requirements or high-rise building structures favor this arrangement.
uses: Information exchange within very small groups
cross_refs: New offices for the Federal Environment Office, Dessau, Sauerbruch, Hutton (→)

fichas.title: Reversible offices
fichas.summary: Reversible offices were an attempt to improve open-plan working conditions by allowing partitions to create a more effective single-room or cubicle layout when concentrated work was needed. The text notes the increased technical input required for flexibility and describes how user dissatisfaction, energy costs, and new technologies contributed to the form being questioned.

fichas.title: Group-room offices
fichas.summary: Group rooms, described as smaller open-plan arrangements, suit work groups that exchange information constantly. They seek to allow more individual choice and improve light, air, and individuality. The text says full air conditioning may be omitted in favor of back-up ventilation, opening windows, and radiators. Linked and partially zoned group rooms may connect through reversible small-room zones and be zoned for common areas when required.
uses: Work by groups with constant information exchange
Partially zoning linked rooms for common areas
